rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords need an at-fault or no-fault just cause to end a covered tenancy. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay relocation assistance of two months' rent (three if tenant is senior 62+ or disabled), by payment or rent waiver.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation 2 months' rent (3 months if senior or disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies over 30 days in residential rental property
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing, dorms, owner-occupied single-family (up to 2 rented units/rooms) or owner-occupied duplex, separately alienable unit with non-corporate owner and written notice, certificate of occupancy within 15 years, transient hotels, nonprofit/care facilities, mobilehomes under MRL
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2
rules.interaction: Consistent with state Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2; adds local relocation and buyout rules.

notes: Legal-aid FAQ updated 2023-09-21. Page does not mention rent control or rent caps (only refers to Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 in the required notice); it does not say San Diego has no rent control. Section cites on the page: 98.0705, 98.0706.
